emerging_technology: Agentic AI (same broad technology category in all three cases; assess a specific usable system and do not generalize to all AI)
intended_application: A hypothetical consulting firm is considering an internal knowledge-search and briefing assistant. It would retrieve and summarize firm-approved internal material and draft briefings for consultants; a human consultant would review and approve every briefing before it is used or shared.
organization: A hypothetical consulting firm with distributed teams, a large internal knowledge repository, and client-specific workspaces.
business_need: Help consultants find relevant internal knowledge more efficiently and prepare first-draft briefings while preserving professional review and client confidentiality.
users_stakeholders: Consultants, project managers, knowledge-management staff, information-security staff, and clients whose confidential information may be stored in project workspaces.
adoption_posture: Cautious and exploratory: the firm is considering a small internal test with human review and restricted data access.
capabilities_constraints: For this hypothetical case, assume the firm has an internal knowledge-management function and a small technology team, but no supplied evaluation of agent accuracy, retrieval quality, integration effort, or handling of confidential material.
risk_consequence_context: Incorrect summaries could mislead consultants; unauthorized access or disclosure could expose confidential client information; poor source attribution could undermine trust. Human review is required, and the case provides no measured evidence that review eliminates these risks.
management_question: What is justified about the general significance of Agentic AI, how consequential is this internal knowledge-search application, and what should this firm's posture mean for its current evaluation of the use case?
time_horizon: Assess the technology using current, dated evidence; the firm is considering whether to begin a controlled internal test during the next 12 months.
additional_context: This is a fictional scenario, not a claim that a particular consulting firm or system exists or has achieved these outcomes. Keep the broad technology category constant with the other cases. The application and organizational consequences differ from the retailer case; do not let the firm's cautious posture change general technology evidence. Research context to verify and weigh: NIST (2025-08-05) describes AI-agent systems as models with software scaffolding for tool use and distinguishes tool permissions, including read-only retrieval and constrained writing; read-only retrieval alone does not establish agentic behavior: https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2025/08/lessons-learned-consortium-tool-use-agent-systems. McKinsey's 2026-08-25 global survey reports that about two in ten respondents say their organizations have reached the scaling phase with AI agents, and reports knowledge management among functions where agent use is reported; these are respondent-reported survey findings, not deployment logs or performance evidence for this particular briefing use: https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/quantumblack/our-insights/the-state-of-ai. Counterevidence and limits: METR's task-horizon measurement, last updated 2026-05-08, is based mainly on well-specified software, machine-learning, and cybersecurity tasks; it explicitly cautions that task horizon does not mean an agent can autonomously perform an equivalent duration of professional work, and performance drops on messier, holistic tasks: https://metr.org/time-horizons/. No source supplied here verifies the accuracy, citation fidelity, or confidentiality controls of the hypothetical assistant. Treat all case details as hypothetical; verify any additional current claims against original sources.
